title: Variant bridge and deprecation safeguard playbook for pinned model versions
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers pin model versions for stability; when a pinned variant is retired or becomes incompatible, we currently have brittle fallbacks that either increase latency or silently change model semantics. This ticket designs an operator-facing and automated fallback policy that preserves semantics, manages regional constraints, and provides clear deprecation signals to customers.

Scope:
- Define a configurable 'variant bridge' layer that can attempt compatibility-preserving substitutions for pinned model versions across regions and quantization variants.
- Specify deprecation handling flow: pre-deprecation telemetry, customer notification windows, warmup and cache-priming, and graceful retirement.
- Provide operator runbooks and consoles hooks (rollback, force-evict, escalate) and automated metrics/alerts.
- Implement compatibility scoring (semantic + API surface + perf delta) and cost/latency-aware weighting for fallback decisions.
- Publish a small set of API/manifest keys customers can set on their pins (max_fallback_hops, prefer_region_local, cost_threshold_usd, semantic_tolerance).

Design highlights: 
1) Compatibility score: numeric 0..100 combining model ABI check (tokenizer + shape + special tokens), structured-output schema check, and quality regression estimate from historical evals. Substitutions require score >= configurable threshold (default 80).
2) Prioritization policy: prefer same-architecture variants (e.g., fp16 -> q4_0) in same region, then same model family in same region, then remote-region with latency budget check. Each candidate gets a weighted score that includes compatibility, regional-slo-penalty, and per-token-cost delta.
3) Soft deprecation window: 
   - T-30d: telemetry flagging + recommend warmup schedule to customers via console and email.
   - T-14d: optional canary substitution for low-traffic customers (customer opt-in), start KV cache prefill for likely prefixes.
   - T-3d: automatic agent-run warmup for critical paths and final compatibility validations.
   - T-0: begin phased traffic redirection with decreasing weight to retiring variant, automatic rollback if QA metrics deviate beyond thresholds.
4) Fallback orchestration: implement as a policy engine with these config knobs: max_fallback_hops, allow_cross_region (bool), backoff-on-latency (ms), prefer_cached_variant (bool), dynamic_rebalance_window. Engine emits deterministic decision logs to allow replay and audit.
5) Observability & SLOs: new dashboard 'Pinned Fallbacks' showing fallback rate, median extra-latency, semantic-regression-rate (from eval set), and customer-facing incident timeline. Alert if fallback rate > 0.5% globally or > 2% for a single customer for > 15m.

Operator runbook (high level):
- When retirement is scheduled, verify candidate pool, run compatibility cohort tests, notify customers.
- If high semantic drift detected after substitution, trigger immediate weighted rollback and open Priority Incident.
- For cross-region shifts, ensure KV prefix warmup and pre-warm replication to avoid cold-KV miss spikes.

APIs & manifests: propose pin manifest additions:
- pin_config.max_fallback_hops (int)
- pin_config.prefer_region_local (enum: strict|soft|none)
- pin_config.semantic_tolerance (float 0..1)
- pin_config.notify_emails (list)

Testing plan: unit tests for policy engine scoring, e2e sim that runs traffic through synthetic pins and retires variants to validate rollback triggers, canary experiments across a subset of customers, and chaos tests that simulate region outage + retirement.

Risks & tradeoffs: prioritizing semantic fidelity can increase cost/latency if we must pick heavyweight variants; we mitigate this with cost-aware weighting and per-customer thresholds. Cross-region fallbacks add complexity around KV cache coherence and compliance — allow disabling per-pin or per-customer.

Deliverables: design doc (Confluence link), policy engine proto + controller, new pin manifest fields, console UI for pin lifecycle, operator runbook, dashboards and alerts.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine prototype that can evaluate candidate variants and return deterministic fallback decisions (unit-tested)
Pin manifest schema updated and backward-compatible with default values
E2E sim verifying rollback triggers when semantic-regression-rate exceeds threshold
Console UI surface to schedule deprecations and show per-customer fallback audit logs
Dashboard and alerting for fallback rate and extra-latency metrics
Operator runbook published and reviewed by SRE and Support
